boxes_method: Hand-annotated on 2x zooms with a pixel grid, guided by a groove-detection pass (local-darkness threshold + connected components). One box per carved letter group (a consonant with its attached vowel signs). Verified by rendering design/hero/boxes-overlay.jpg.

glyphs.method: Reader.read_glyphs: per row, the clean crop and the crop with numbered boxes (design/hero/boxes.json) in one vision call; the model names the modern Tamil letter in each box with its probability that the letter is right

The hero shows this letter-by-letter reading: for each hand-drawn box, the modern Tamil letter the Reader named and its own probability that the letter is right (self-reported, not calibrated). Letters it named under 0.5 were treated as gaps and sent to the Restorer.

restore.config: deployed (config/models.yaml after PR #40): restorer.strategy_llm prerank, ngram_prerank true, VAL-fitted Platt calibration (src/ezhuthu/agent/calibration.json); no Strands Decider call for restoration
restore.note: EzhuthuService.restore with the deployed configuration: the LLM's candidate fills, DHARMA parallels and the character 5-gram are pre-ranked (noisy-OR), then the top score is mapped to a calibrated confidence fitted on VAL. The gap is filled only if that confidence reaches the calibration's own threshold (abstain_below per gap); here the best fill scored under it, so the gap is left open. Re-run 2026-11-02 after PR #40; it replaces an earlier run whose fills were ranked by the hosted Strands Decider v19 (restorer.strategy_llm noul-topk) against a flat 0.5.

line_reading.note: The app's own line-by-line reading of the same crop (Sonnet 4.6, then Opus 4.6 on 'read again'), and the Restorer on its gaps (with the superseded noul-topk config). Kept for the record; the hero shows the letter-by-letter reading.

interpret.method: Interpreter.interpret (src/ezhuthu/agent/interpreter.py) on the letter-by-letter reading (runs/glyphs.json) with the Restorer's decisions (runs/restore.json)
interpret.context: A crop of four lines from a longer Chola-period inscription on the wall of the Brihadisvara temple, Thanjavur; the text runs on beyond the left and right edges of the crop, so the first and last words of a line may be cut.
interpret.meaning_en: This is a fragment of a donative record: a tank (kuḷam) is to be given (koṭum) for a settlement (kuṭi); the surrounding text is too fragmentary to read fully.
interpret.meaning_ta: இது ஒரு தானக் கல்வெட்டின் துண்டு: ஒரு குடிக்கு குளம் கொடுக்கப்படும் என்று கூறுகிறது; மற்ற பகுதிகள் தெளிவற்றவை.
interpret.notes: Letters 1.1–1.5 and most of lines 2–3 are very uncertain; the hint words 'kuṭikku' and 'kuḷam' are the most reliable anchors. The unread letter 3.2 and the low-confidence matches in lines 2 and 4 make the surrounding context unclear.
interpret.note: Words, phrase and meaning by Ezhuthu's Interpreter (src/ezhuthu/agent/interpreter.py): the model divided the letters into words (naming each word's letters), spelled them in today's Tamil and said what they mean, grounded with words attested in the DHARMA train split and the ontology. Probabilities are the model's own (not calibrated). No edition exists to check it against (see edition_note), so the hero credits the meaning to Ezhuthu.

edition_note: This stone is not identified in DHARMA or another published edition we could find, so the hero shows no edition text and no match rate, and the meaning is credited to Ezhuthu. Searches of Wikimedia Commons for an openly licensed photo of an inscription in the DHARMA train split (2026-11-02, twice) found none whose text could be matched to an edition: the two closest candidates (Airavatesvara temple, Darasuram) were read by the Reader as Vatteluttu / illegible and could not be tied to DHARMA_INSTamilNadu00619, 00602 or 00603.

live_calls.note: Bedrock calls. Reader: includes a Sonnet+Opus read of a 6-line crop of the same photo that was not used. Glyphs: one Opus call per row. Restorer: 6 on the line reading (two runs), 1 on the letter-by-letter reading with the old noul-topk config, and 1 (Opus, pre-escalated) re-running it with the deployed prerank config. Interpreter: Sonnet then Opus (Sonnet was under 0.6), twice; the first pair used a prompt without a length limit on the meaning and was superseded. Photo search: Reader calls on two candidate photos that were not used. The superseded restorer run also called the hosted Strands Decider API (not Bedrock); the deployed config makes no decider call.
